en: 10. Indriyayamaka 10.3.
The Section on Full Understanding (Pariññāvāra) 10.3.2.
The Section on the Past (Atītavāra)
10.3.2.1. Positive Order (Anuloma) He who had fully understood the eye-faculty (cakkhundriya) had abandoned the faculty of mental grief (domanassindriya), did he not? Yes.
Or rather, he who had abandoned the faculty of mental grief had fully understood the eye-faculty, had he not? Yes.

Two types of persons have abandoned the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*), but they have not fully understood the faculty of the eye (*cakkhundriya*). An Arhat has both abandoned the faculty of mental grief and fully understood the faculty of the eye.
He who has fully understood the faculty of the eye, has he cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*)? Yes.
Or rather, he who has cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," has he fully understood the faculty of the eye?

Six persons have cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," but they have not fully understood the eye-faculty. An Arhat has both cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" and fully understood the eye-faculty.
Is it the case that whoever has fully understood the eye-faculty has cultivated the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*)? Yes.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever has cultivated the faculty of final knowledge has fully understood the eye-faculty? Yes.
Is it the case that whoever had fully understood the eye-faculty (cakkhundriya) has realized the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya)?
Whoever realizes the fruit of the highest attainment (aggaphala) has fully understood the eye-faculty, but has not realized the faculty of one who has already known.
Whoever has realized the fruit of the highest attainment has both fully understood the eye-faculty and realized the faculty of one who has already known.
Or, whoever had realized the faculty of one who has known, had he also fully understood the faculty of the eye? Yes. (Based on the faculty of the eye.
Whoever had abandoned the faculty of mental grief, had he also cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"? Yes.
Or, whoever had cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," had he also abandoned the faculty of mental grief?

Four persons have cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," but they have not abandoned the faculty of mental distress. Three persons have both cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" and abandoned the faculty of mental distress.
Is it the case that whoever has abandoned the faculty of mental distress has also cultivated the faculty of final knowledge?

Two persons have abandoned the faculty of mental distress, but they have not cultivated the faculty of final knowledge. An arahant has both abandoned the faculty of mental distress and cultivated the faculty of final knowledge.
Or, whoever has cultivated the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*), has he abandoned the faculty of mental distress (*domanassindriya*)? Yes.
Whoever has abandoned the faculty of mental distress, has he realized the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*)?

Three types of persons have abandoned the faculty of mental distress, but they have not realized the faculty of one who has already known. The Arhat has both abandoned the faculty of mental distress and realized the faculty of one who has already known.
Or, whoever had realized the faculty of one who has already known, had he abandoned the faculty of mental distress? Yes. (Based on the faculty of mental distress.
Whoever had cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," had he cultivated the faculty of final knowledge?

Six types of persons had cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," but they had not cultivated the faculty of final knowledge. An Arhat had cultivated both the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" and the faculty of final knowledge.
Or again: Whoever has cultivated the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*) has also cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*)? Yes.
Whoever has cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" has realized the faculty of one who has known (*aññātāvindriya*)?

Seven types of persons have cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," but they have not realized the faculty of one who has known. An Arhat has both cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" and realized the faculty of one who has known.

Or rather: whoever has realized the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya), has he developed the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya)? Yes. (Based on the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Whoever has developed the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya), has he realized the faculty of one who has already known?

Whoever realizes the supreme fruit (aggaphala) has developed the faculty of final knowledge, but has not realized the faculty of one who has already known. Whoever has fully realized the supreme fruit has both developed the faculty of final knowledge and realized the faculty of one who has already known.
Or, whoever has realized the *aññātāvindriya*, has he cultivated the *aññindriya*? Yes. (Based on the *aññindriya*.
10.3.2.2. Negative (Paccanīka) Whoever has not fully understood the eye-faculty (*cakkhundriya*), has he not abandoned the grief-faculty (*domanassindriya*)?

Two persons have not fully understood the eye-faculty (*cakkhundriya*), yet they have not failed to abandon the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*). Six persons have neither fully understood the eye-faculty nor abandoned the faculty of mental grief.
Or, conversely, whoever has not abandoned the faculty of mental grief has not fully understood the eye-faculty? Yes.
Whoever has not fully understood the eye-faculty has not cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*)?

Six persons did not fully understand the eye-faculty (*cakkhundriya*), yet they did not fail to develop the "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" faculty (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*). Two persons neither fully understood the eye-faculty nor developed the "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" faculty.
Is it the case that whoever did not develop the "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" faculty also did not fully understand the eye-faculty? Yes.
Is it the case that whoever did not fully understand the eye-faculty also did not develop the "final-knowledge" faculty (*aññindriya*)? Yes.
Or, whoever did not develop the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya) did not fully understand the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriya)? Yes.
Whoever did not fully understand the faculty of the eye did not realize the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya)? Yes.
Or, whoever did not realize the faculty of one who has already known did not fully understand the faculty of the eye?

He who realizes the fruit of Arhatship (aggaphala) has not previously realized the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya), but he has not failed to fully understand the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriya).
Eight types of persons have neither realized the faculty of one who has already known nor have they fully understood the faculty of the eye.
(Based on the faculty of the eye.)
Is it the case that whoever had not abandoned the faculty of mental distress (domanassindriya) had also not cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya)?

Four types of persons had not abandoned the faculty of mental distress, yet they had not failed to cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown. Two types of persons had neither abandoned the faculty of mental distress nor cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Conversely, is it the case that whoever had not cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" had also not abandoned the faculty of mental distress? Yes, it is so.
He who had not abandoned the faculty of mental distress had not cultivated the faculty of final knowledge? Yes.
Or, he who had not cultivated the faculty of final knowledge had not abandoned the faculty of mental distress?

Two persons had not cultivated the faculty of final knowledge, but they had not failed to abandon the faculty of mental distress. Six persons had neither cultivated the faculty of final knowledge nor abandoned the faculty of mental distress.
Is it the case that whoever had not abandoned the faculty of mental distress (domanassindriya) had also not realized the faculty of one who has known (aññātāvindriya)? Yes.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever had not realized the faculty of one who has known had also not abandoned the faculty of mental distress?
Three types of persons had not realized the faculty of one who has known, yet they had not failed to abandon the faculty of mental distress.
Six persons neither realized the faculty of one who has known nor abandoned the faculty of mental grief.
(Based on the faculty of mental grief.
Whoever did not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" did not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge? Yes.
Or again, whoever did not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*) did not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*)?

Six persons did not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge, but they did not fail to cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown. Two persons neither cultivated the faculty of final knowledge nor did they cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Whoever did not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" did not realize the faculty of one who has known (*aññātāvindriya*)? Yes.
Or again, whoever did not realize the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya), did he not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya)?
Seven persons did not realize the faculty of one who has already known, but they did not fail to develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Two persons neither realized the faculty of one who has already known nor [failed to develop] the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown."
He did not cultivate it. (Based on the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
He who did not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge did not realize the faculty of one who has already known? Yes.
Or rather, he who did not realize the faculty of one who has already known did not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge? Yes.

He who realizes the fruit of Arhatship (aggaphala) has not previously realized the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya), yet it is not the case that he has not cultivated the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya).
Eight types of persons have neither previously realized the faculty of one who has already known nor cultivated the faculty of final knowledge.
(Based on the faculty of final knowledge.)
